title: Hand Signs Between Trusted Colleagues
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Drawing on the covert hand signals baseball coaches use to communicate with players, this piece proposes that leaders and trusted colleagues develop their own private gestures for redirecting behavior in real time without embarrassing anyone. The author catalogs common workplace missteps as prime candidates for a discreet signal rather than a public correction. The piece is explicit that signals should be limited to one or two recurring, individual-specific patterns, and that their power depends on staying undetectable to everyone except the intended recipient.
points: Baseball's covert hand-signal system is offered as a model for leaders who want to redirect a colleague's behavior without a public correction.
Recurring, individual-specific missteps are the best candidates for a private signal rather than open feedback.
Signals should be limited to one or two messages tied to a person's known patterns.
The technique's value depends entirely on discretion, it only works if no one but the intended colleague recognizes what's happening.
quotes: Delivering messages using gestures and distinctive movements is a clever way to communicate with teammates without flagging to others what is being said.
Having a pre-determined gesture that denotes how a colleague or partner should handle a situation or alter their approach can be tremendously powerful.
Colleagues sometimes talk too much or too little, oversell and advocate too strongly, interrupt and talk over others, disclose too much information.
Effective signals between colleagues or partners don’t have to cover more than one or two messages. Reserve them for those infractions that are common patterns for a given individual.
Just remember, no one is supposed to detect the signal except the intended party.
